scenes.tts: Why does a cut-off axon fall apart? Is it starving, or following orders?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Stump That Kills Itself. A cut axon; the distal piece greyed, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Why does a cut-off axon fall apart? Is it starving, or following orders?

scenes.tts: In eighteen fifty, Augustus Waller saw cut frog nerve fibres break up beyond the cut. He read it as a matter of nutrition.
scenes.caption: In 1850, Augustus Waller saw cut frog nerve fibres break up beyond the cut. He read it as a matter of nutrition.
scenes.visual: Credit card: Augustus Waller, 1850. A frog tongue nerve sketch; fibres beyond the cut break up. Label: nutrition?
scenes.narration: In 1850, Augustus Waller saw cut frog nerve fibres break up beyond the cut. He read it as a matter of nutrition.

scenes.tts: If it is starving, only replacing what it lacks should save it. If it is a program, deleting one part should stop it.
scenes.visual: Two columns: starving, only replacing the supply delays it; program, delete one part and it stops.
scenes.narration: If it is starving, only replacing what it lacks should save it. If it is a program, deleting one part should stop it.

scenes.tts: What mouse would decide it?
scenes.visual: A mouse silhouette with a question mark.
scenes.narration: What mouse would decide it?

scenes.tts: One missing a part of the program, whose cut axons stay whole. But the first clue came by accident.
scenes.visual: The mouse silhouette gains a crossed-out gene. Then a schematic plot, labelled schematic time course, not measured percentages: percent of axons intact against days.
scenes.narration: One missing a part of the program, whose cut axons stay whole. But the first clue came by accident.

scenes.tts: In the slow mouse, cut axons last two weeks or more.
scenes.caption: In the slow mouse, Wlds, cut axons last two weeks or more.
scenes.visual: On the schematic plot: wild type falls around 1.5 to 2 days; the Wlds line falls far later, after day 14.
scenes.narration: In the slow mouse, Wlds, cut axons last two weeks or more.

scenes.tts: Its mutation makes an odd fusion with an enzyme that makes N A D plus. Remember that enzyme.
scenes.caption: Its mutation makes an odd fusion with an enzyme that makes NAD+. Remember that enzyme.
scenes.visual: A fusion bar: Ube4b start joined to NMNAT1. Label: makes NAD+.
scenes.narration: Its mutation makes an odd fusion with an enzyme that makes NAD+. Remember that enzyme.

scenes.tts: So it might replace what the stump lacks. That alone cannot prove a program.
scenes.visual: The fusion bar slides into the starving column: it could replace the supply. Label: not yet proof of a program.
scenes.narration: So it might replace what the stump lacks. That alone cannot prove a program.

scenes.tts: Then came the deciding mouse. Mice lacking an ordinary gene, Sarm one, kept cut axons intact for a long time. The stump carries a program.
scenes.caption: Then came the deciding mouse. Mice lacking an ordinary gene, Sarm1, kept cut axons intact for a long time. The stump carries a program.
scenes.visual: A second late-falling schematic line is added: Sarm1-null. Credit: Freeman laboratory and collaborators, 2012. The gene moves to the program column. Label: a program.
scenes.narration: Then came the deciding mouse. Mice lacking an ordinary gene, Sarm1, kept cut axons intact for a long time. The stump carries a program.

scenes.tts: Why is a long axon so exposed? Picture a metre-long axon, ten micrometres wide, holding about a thousand times the volume of a cell body fifty micrometres wide. It depends on deliveries from that body.
scenes.caption: Why is a long axon so exposed? Picture a metre-long axon, 10 micrometres wide, holding about a thousand times the volume of a cell body 50 micrometres wide. It depends on deliveries from that body.
scenes.visual: A small sphere labelled cell body, 50 µm across, beside a long cylinder labelled axon, 1 m long and 10 µm wide; label: approximate shapes. On screen: about 1,000 times the volume. A conveyor carries parcels down the axon.
scenes.narration: Why is a long axon so exposed? Picture a metre-long axon, 10 micrometres wide, holding about a thousand times the volume of a cell body 50 micrometres wide. It depends on deliveries from that body.

scenes.tts: The key delivery is N M N A T two, the least stable enzyme of its family. It turns N M N, nicotinamide mononucleotide, into N A D plus.
scenes.caption: The key delivery is NMNAT2, the least stable enzyme of its family. It turns NMN, nicotinamide mononucleotide, into NAD+.
scenes.visual: Label: NMNAT2, least stable. Reaction on screen: NMN (nicotinamide mononucleotide) to NAD+.
scenes.narration: The key delivery is NMNAT2, the least stable enzyme of its family. It turns NMN, nicotinamide mononucleotide, into NAD+.

scenes.tts: The slow mouse's fusion protein is a longer-lived N M N A T. It keeps that job going after a cut.
scenes.caption: The slow mouse's fusion protein is a longer-lived NMNAT. It keeps that job going after a cut.
scenes.visual: The Wlds fusion bar returns beside the conveyor; after the cut it keeps making NAD+. Label: longer-lived NMNAT activity.
scenes.narration: The slow mouse's fusion protein is a longer-lived NMNAT. It keeps that job going after a cut.

scenes.tts: After a cut, it stops arriving. What happens to N M N, and to N A D plus?
scenes.caption: After a cut, it stops arriving. What happens to NMN, and to NAD+?
scenes.visual: The conveyor is cut; the NMNAT2 bar falls. A gauge with two needles, NMN and NAD+, and a question mark.
scenes.narration: After a cut, it stops arriving. What happens to NMN, and to NAD+?

scenes.tts: N M N piles up, and N A D plus falls. Their ratio climbs as the enzyme fails.
scenes.caption: NMN piles up, and NAD+ falls. Their ratio climbs as the enzyme fails.
scenes.visual: The NMN needle rises; the NAD+ needle falls. Label: the NMN to NAD+ ratio rises after NMNAT2 loss; NMN supply and NAD+ use also move it.
scenes.narration: NMN piles up, and NAD+ falls. Their ratio climbs as the enzyme fails.

scenes.tts: Sarm one senses that ratio. It is a ring of eight, held off while N A D plus is bound.
scenes.caption: SARM1 senses that ratio. It is a ring of eight, held off while NAD+ is bound.
scenes.visual: A central ring of eight SARM1 units, with ARM domains on the outside holding NAD+, and TIR domains kept apart.
scenes.narration: SARM1 senses that ratio. It is a ring of eight, held off while NAD+ is bound.

scenes.tts: In the leading model, N M N competes for that site. Its binding shifts the outer domains and frees the T I R domains.
scenes.caption: In the leading model, NMN competes for that site. Its binding shifts the outer domains and frees the TIR domains.
scenes.visual: NMN replaces NAD+ at the outer ARM sites. The central ring stays intact; the ARM domains shift and the TIR domains are released. Label: leading model.
scenes.narration: In the leading model, NMN competes for that site. Its binding shifts the outer domains and frees the TIR domains.

scenes.tts: The freed T I R domains come together into an enzyme that cleaves N A D plus. In this model, each loss may push the ratio higher, and the slow drift becomes a crash.
scenes.caption: The freed TIR domains come together into an enzyme that cleaves NAD+. In this model, each loss may push the ratio higher, and the slow drift becomes a crash.
scenes.visual: The TIR domains come together and cut NAD+. A loop arrow, labelled proposed feedback: less NAD+, higher ratio, more SARM1 activity. The NAD+ bar crashes.
scenes.narration: The freed TIR domains come together into an enzyme that cleaves NAD+. In this model, each loss may push the ratio higher, and the slow drift becomes a crash.

scenes.tts: Energy fails, calcium rises, and calpains, proteases switched on by calcium, cut the cytoskeleton.
scenes.visual: The ATP bar falls; calcium floods in; calpain scissors cut the cytoskeleton; the axon fragments.
scenes.narration: Energy fails, calcium rises, and calpains, proteases switched on by calcium, cut the cytoskeleton.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking N M N A T two from the start die around birth. Their growing axons stall. Remove Sarm one too. What happens?
scenes.caption: Mice lacking NMNAT2 from the start die around birth. Their growing axons stall. Remove Sarm1 too. What happens?
scenes.visual: A table builds, labelled development: NMNAT2-deficient, axon growth stalls, die around birth. A new row, NMNAT2-deficient and Sarm1-null, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking NMNAT2 from the start die around birth. Their growing axons stall. Remove Sarm1 too. What happens?

scenes.tts: Their axons grow, and the mice survive. Losing N M N A T two works by tripping Sarm one.
scenes.caption: Their axons grow, and the mice survive. Losing NMNAT2 works by tripping SARM1.
scenes.visual: The last row fills: axons grow, mice survive. Arrow: NMNAT2 loss acts through SARM1.
scenes.narration: Their axons grow, and the mice survive. Losing NMNAT2 works by tripping SARM1.

scenes.tts: And it is not apoptosis. The stump degenerates even when caspases are blocked.
scenes.visual: Label: not apoptosis. Caspase icons crossed out; the stump still fragments.
scenes.narration: And it is not apoptosis. The stump degenerates even when caspases are blocked.

scenes.tts: So the cut-off piece is not simply starving. It carries a switch that waits for the deliveries to stop.
scenes.visual: Closing card: a switch that waits for the deliveries to stop.
scenes.narration: So the cut-off piece is not simply starving. It carries a switch that waits for the deliveries to stop.
